newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty urges Albania to respect human rights.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty urges Albania to respect human rights.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Monday that Albania's declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on civil liberties risked paving the way to increased violations of human rights.
"It is clearly the duty of the authorities to bring an end to the civil disturbances that have broken out," the London-based human rights organisation said in a statement.
"But the authorities should reduce to the minimum restrictions on civil liberties and seek a way out of conflict through peaceful negotiation."
Amnesty noted that Albania has signed key human rights treaties which state that even at times of emergency certain human rights, such as the rights to life and freedom from torture, are sacrosanct.

Albania imposed a state of emergency and nationwide curfew on Monday in response to armed unrest in the south of the country. Albanians have been angered by the loss of their savings in pyramid investment schemes which collapsed.
Amnesty criticised emergency provisions which authorise security forces to open fire without warning at people who fail to hand in their arms.

"These provisions are open to abuse in circumstances where fears and passions are inflamed and in which security forces with insufficient training are confronted with the difficult task of imposing order," Amnesty said.
Amnesty urged the Albanian authorities to ensure that security forces are instructed to observe international standards of law enforcement as set out by the United Nations.
It said there had been a disturbing series of allegations that that government opponents had been attacked by men in plain clothes apparently linked to the security forces.
The organisation said it wanted to remind the Albanian authorities that torture and ill-treatment are internationally banned under all circumstances, including states of emergency.
Amnesty said it was disturbed by the introduction of censorship and a ban on public gatherings by the Albanian authorites.
